title: A Lissajous Figure-Eight from x = sin t, y = sin 2t
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Graph the Lissajous curve x = sin t, y = sin 2t for 0 <= t <= 2*pi. Describe its shape, test it for symmetry, and find an algebraic relation between x and y that the curve satisfies.
finalAnswer: y^2 = 4x^2(1 - x^2) \quad (\text{figure-eight, symmetric about the origin and both axes})

steps.title: Use the double-angle identity
steps.explanation: Because x = sin t, the y-coordinate factors as twice x times cos t, linking the two coordinates directly.
steps.why: Rewriting y in terms of x and the remaining trig function is the standard route to eliminating the parameter.

steps.title: Eliminate t
steps.explanation: Squaring removes the sign of cos t, so the whole curve lies on the algebraic set y^2 = 4x^2(1 - x^2) with |x| <= 1.
steps.why: Squaring is necessary here because one value of x corresponds to two values of cos t, which is precisely why the curve doubles back on itself.

steps.title: Read the shape and symmetry
steps.explanation: Replacing t by t + pi sends (x, y) to (-x, -y), giving origin symmetry, and the relation is unchanged when x or y alone is negated, so the plot is a figure-eight crossing itself at the origin (t = 0, pi, 2*pi).
steps.why: Symmetry checks let you plot only part of the curve and confirm that the software's output is not distorted.

steps.title: Pick the window
steps.explanation: Since |x| <= 1 and |y| <= 1, a slightly padded square window with equal scaling captures both lobes and keeps the crossing at the origin visible.
steps.why: A non-square aspect ratio would visually stretch one lobe and hide the balanced eight shape.
